solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Romans insist on changing conveyance

indicators.note: letters that are changing are being altered into a different order

blocks.note: both words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans demanding a particular form of transport or carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans insist on changing' reads like a historical demand, but the two words supply all twelve letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmission is the act of passing something along or carrying it from place to place, which is one sense of conveyance.

clue.text: Road sweeping price

blocks.note: a sweeping search is a thorough one
a fare is the price of a journey

explanation.surface: The cost of having a street cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road sweeping' suggests street cleaning, but 'sweeping' is an adjective meaning complete, and 'price' is a ticket cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main public street or route through a town, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A boxing contest is concerning

blocks.note: taken as written
a single fight or match in the ring

explanation.surface: Someone finds a prize fight worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like an adjective meaning worrying, but here it is the preposition meaning on the subject of.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, both words mean regarding or on the topic of, as in a book about birds.

clue.text: Pulls small locomotives

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
locomotives haul trains, standing in for them here

explanation.surface: Little engines hauling loads along a track.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Pulls' the action of the engines, but it is the definition, as in pulling a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain a muscle is to pull it, so both verbs describe overstretching or tugging hard.

clue.text: Popular act without doubt

blocks.note: something popular is in fashion, or in
a deed is an act or action

explanation.surface: A performer who is certainly a crowd favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' suggests a stage turn, but it is an action, a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb of emphasis meaning certainly or truly, matching the phrase for certainty.

clue.text: Pointed tip of short instrument

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very end point, here the leading letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Describing the sharpened end of a small tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a tool with a point, but it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and pointed are both adjectives for an edge or tip able to pierce or cut.

clue.text: Exile unpopular group of actors

blocks.note: out of favour or fashion, the opposite of in
the cast is the company of performers in a show

explanation.surface: An instruction to banish a disliked theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exile' reads as a verb, but the definition is the noun: a person who has been banished.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected or driven out by society, which is what an exile is.

clue.text: Fulfilled expert

blocks.note: first meaning: achieved or completed
second meaning: highly skilled

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that read like a description of a satisfied professional are separate senses of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A task carried out is achieved or completed, and a person who is highly skilled and talented is also described this way.

clue.text: Old, dismal scent

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
dour means gloomy or sullen

explanation.surface: A stale, depressing smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Old' and 'dismal' look like a pair of adjectives describing the smell; each supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, so it is a near synonym for scent, although usually less pleasant.

clue.text: Radical doctor having wine with bit of cocaine

indicators.note: a bit is a small fragment, so only a single letter is taken, the opening one

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
the opening letter of the drug

explanation.surface: An extreme medic drinking and taking a little cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical doctor' looks like one phrase, but 'Radical' is the definition on its own. Asti is a crossword favourite among wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic and radical both describe measures that are extreme, far-reaching and severe in effect.

clue.text: Survive abroad with pounds I have

blocks.note: out means away from home, as abroad does
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
contracted as I've

explanation.surface: Someone managing to get by overseas on their own money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Survive abroad' suggests living overseas, but 'Survive' alone is the definition and 'abroad' gives the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlive is to live longer than someone or something, which is a transitive sense of survive.

clue.text: Philosopher not working in unit of US soldiers

indicators.note: not means without, so a word is taken out of a longer one

blocks.note: a platoon is a small military unit
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A thinker who is idle while serving in an American army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a philosopher off duty, but 'not working' tells you to remove the word for working from the end of the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek thinker, a student of Socrates, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: Showy decoration lacking hint of nuance

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so something is dropped
a hint is the merest trace, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: a garnish is decoration on a plate of food
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Flashy ornamentation with no subtlety at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showy decoration' looks like a single phrase; 'Showy' alone is the definition, and the decoration is the culinary kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy, loud and over-bright, which is the unflattering sense of being flamboyant to look at.

clue.text: Tell heads of regional engineering company of unusual new technology

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so each word yields its leading letter

blocks.clueFragment: regional engineering company of unusual new technology
blocks.note: the opening letters of all seven words, including the little word in the middle

explanation.surface: Bosses of a local engineering firm describing a strange invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' suggests company bosses, but it means first letters; do not skip the small word 'of', which supplies a letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to narrate or relate it, which is one sense of the verb tell.

clue.text: Warm male with a sheep

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
taken as written
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A cosy farmer huddled up with a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a British dialect and farming word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat up something is to make it warm, so the phrasal verb and the verb match.

clue.text: Turned without resistance and developed

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: revolved means turned round
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Something that changed course unopposed and grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without resistance' reads as easily, but resistance is the physics symbol R, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually, so evolved and developed are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Period of time before non-disclosure agreement programme

blocks.note: an age is an era or period
NDA is the standard initialism for a non-disclosure agreement

explanation.surface: A schedule with a waiting period before a confidentiality deal is signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' simply places one piece ahead of the other in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done, a sense shared with a programme of events.

clue.text: Confronts first of famous champions

indicators.note: first of a word means its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
aces are experts or champions

explanation.surface: Someone taking on the leading star among sporting greats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confronts' is the verb definition; 'champions' are top performers, not supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a challenge or opponent is to confront it, so the third-person verbs match.

clue.text: Toss coins for young family member

indicators.note: tossing things throws them about so they land in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Flipping a coin to decide something for a child in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin toss is the scene; 'Toss' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a descendant or heir, especially a younger member of a notable family.

clue.text: Try holding new chic remodelled Italian dish

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece sits within another
something remodelled has been reshaped into a different form

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sampling a trendy, reinvented Italian recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New chic' looks like a fashion phrase, but the first word goes inside 'Try' and the second is shuffled and added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings, usually made of potato, served as a pasta course.

clue.text: Charlie and son cover up smell for friends

indicators.note: covering something up surrounds it, so two outer letters wrap round a word

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
S is the abbreviation for son
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A father and son hiding a bad smell from their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum is informal British for a stink, as in 'there's a hum in here'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chums is informal British English for close pals or companions, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ruin one strange gathering of old friends

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd get-together of former pals that someone spoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it is simply letters for rearranging along with 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion is a meeting of people, such as former classmates, who have not seen each other in years.

clue.text: Support from Victor accompanied by expression of pain

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ouch is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: A man named Victor offering help while wincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a person's name but is the radio code word for a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch for someone is to back them up or confirm their honesty, so both verbs mean endorse.

clue.text: Uniform is rumpled, sad and tired after start of shift

indicators.note: rumpled clothes are crumpled out of shape, so the letters are messed into a new order
the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
three words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker's outfit looks crumpled and they feel weary once the shift begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like the clothing noun, but it is the adjective meaning all alike. 'After' places the rearranged letters behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are standardised have been made consistent, regular and the same throughout, which is what uniform means as an adjective.
